gettingThere.fromTerminal: Most cruise ships use the Royal Cruise Berth on the Honnørkajen waterfront, within walking distance of the city centre. Some sailings list Berth 4110 instead—check your daily programme and cruise documents before you leave the ship.

gettingThere.publicTransport: Walking is practical when ships are alongside the waterfront. Aalborg railway station is a short taxi or bus ride from the port—use Rejseplanen or DSB for live times on your call date. Aalborg Airport (AAL) is a separate transfer; allow extra time with luggage.

thingsToDo.intro: Plan one neighbourhood cluster and leave time to get back through port security. The Honnørkajen waterfront and historic centre are the easiest wins on a typical call.

thingsToDo.standardCall: You can combine a museum visit, lunch in the centre, Budolfi Cathedral, and a waterfront loop on a typical six-to-eight-hour call. Check opening times before you commit, and start your return well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: With eight hours or more, consider Lindholm Høje or a second museum only if you have confirmed bus or taxi timings and a clear path back. On overnight calls, reconfirm reboarding rules with the ship.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Check whether your sailing lists Royal Cruise Berth or Berth 4110 before you choose a return landmark—occasional ships use the alternate berth.

portInfo.description: The three headline cultural stops explain different parts of Abu Dhabi. Each deserves time rather than being reduced to a car-window photograph. Arrival is through Zayed Port. The passenger terminal dates to 2015, Marsa Mina was developed in 2019, and Cruise Terminal 2 opened in Q4 2022. Sir Bani Yas Cruise Beach belongs to the emirate’s western island coast, not this city’s cruise-terminal inventory.

Louvre Abu Dhabi, Saadiyat Cultural District: allow 2–3 hours for galleries and architecture, reached by vehicle, not a presumed short waterfront walk. Confirm ticket/closure information directly; the first-party museum page was challenge-blocked, while DCT’s destination listing was captured.

Marsa Mina, beside the passenger terminal: 30–45 minutes of waterfront retail/refreshments, useful if arrival is delayed. Obtain the safe route from the assigned terminal, especially T2.

Corniche Beach, a defined meeting point at Al Sahil Gate 4 on Corniche Road: 60 minutes for a promenade break rather than assuming every beach section is free or equally accessible. DCT describes several sections; recheck swimming conditions.

portInfo.description: Founded by Alexander in 331 BC, Alexandria became the seat of Ptolemaic rule. The Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities explains its later Roman and Byzantine urban remains, including Kom el-Dikka’s theatre, baths and lecture spaces. The modern Bibliotheca is a library-and-museum cultural complex, not the surviving ancient library. Keeping those periods distinct makes a more rewarding visit than a generic “Egypt highlights” drive. The important shore-day choice is local Alexandria versus Cairo/Giza. Neither a cruise-terminal berth total nor the physical possibility of a highway journey proves that the latter fits your all-aboard. This guide prioritises local routes with a generous vehicle return. A distant trip needs the line’s dated excursion duration and delay policy.

Bibliotheca Alexandrina, eastern Corniche: allow 90 minutes for a selective library/cultural-complex visit; check which galleries and museums are open and ticketed.
Kom el-Dikka, central Alexandria: about 90 minutes for the open-air Roman/Byzantine remains, including theatre, baths and mosaics. Sun and uneven paths matter; no unverified accessibility guarantee.
Kom al-Shoqafa catacombs, near the Serapeum: about 75 minutes for the funerary complex; steps/underground access should be checked before booking.
Serapeum/Diocletian’s Column, Alexandria: around 60 minutes; this is the monument popularly called Pompey’s Pillar, with the correct historical identification retained.

portInfo.description: Amsterdam cruise calls commonly use Passenger Terminal Amsterdam (PTA) on the IJ waterfront east of Centraal Station, with some ships using alternative berths or the IJmuiden sea lock complex on certain itineraries. From PTA, trams, metro, ferries, and taxis connect quickly into the historic canal belt.

Betty’s Hope tells a different story:plantation sugar and the people enslaved in its production. Neither should be reduced to a backdrop for beaches. The 2024 tourism guide preserves heritage descriptions and contacts, but is not a current opening calendar. The port website’s technical page genuinely names the local five berths; unrelated template capacity blocks are not taken as Antiguan engineering facts. The destination’s landmark article uses a constructed tourist narrative, which is not a real traveller review and is not reproduced as one.

portInfo.description: Barbados rewards choosing either a city-and-sea day or a focused inland attraction. The Nidhe Israel complex adds Jewish-community history; Pelican Craft Centre makes a local stop directly on the authority’s recommended city walking approach. Kensington Oval’s exterior statue offers cricket context without inventing a stadium-tour admission. The cruise terminal sits within a working port. The authority provides an optional, complimentary berth-dependent ship–terminal shuttle, including wheelchair-accessible units; that does not guarantee a step-free gangway or a free ride into town. The 20-minute city walk in the official text starts at the main gate, via Trevor’s Way and Pelican Craft Centre, not alongside an arbitrary ship berth.

portInfo.description: Dubai’s appeal is the contrast between a trading city around the Creek and newer skyline districts further along the coast. Al Fahidi’s narrow lanes, an abra crossing and Deira’s Gold Souk offer a different day from an observation deck above Downtown or Palm Jumeirah. The official 2026 city guide documents these distinct clusters. Do not spend a four-hour call trying to collect all of them. Mina Rashid has offered homeporting since 2007. Dubai Harbour’s twin-terminal arrival infrastructure began welcoming passengers in 2021. topThings: Creek abra crossing, specifically Bur Dubai Abra Station–Deira Old Souq Abra Station: RTA confirms the route. Allow 45 minutes including finding the jetty, waiting and crossing. Check assistance before choosing a low-sided traditional boat; it is not automatically wheelchair accessible.

Gold Souk, Deira: a market visit rather than a promised bargain; allow 60 minutes after the crossing, with walking time between the landing and market. Use Deira Old Souq Abra Station as an agreed pickup rendezvous, with the market walking leg kept inside the visit allowance.
Burj Khalifa observation decks, Downtown Dubai: allow two hours including ticket and lift queues, plus terminal transfers. Choose a timed slot with slack; a ticket does not secure a return taxi.

The View at The Palm, Palm Jumeirah: a more geographically coherent observation-deck choice from Harbour. Allow 90 minutes and use the venue’s entrance directions rather than a pin on the whole island.

Marina Walk marine-station waterfront, Dubai Marina: a defined starting point for a 60–90-minute promenade/refreshment break, convenient as a Harbour-area option. RTA lists Marina Walk and other Marina stops; do not assume a fixed boat departure without checking its timetable.

portInfo.description: The Port of Fujairah is the UAE’s only multi-purpose seaport on the eastern coastline, about 70 nautical miles outside the Strait of Hormuz. Fujairah Ports Authority describes oil, dry bulk, container, general cargo, passenger/RoRo and marine services. Under a June 2017 35-year concession, AD Ports Group’s Fujairah Terminals upgraded container/general-cargo infrastructure and states it provides Cruise Ship services alongside RoRo and livestock. Terminal capacity targets cited by the authority include 720,000 TEUs and 1.3 million tons of general cargo by 2030. Cruise-specific passenger-hall dimensions and door GPS for the numbered berths were not isolated beyond the main-quay table — treat berth assignment as line-controlled.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Cruise Gate Hamburg operates HafenCity, Altona, Steinwerder, and Baakenhöft
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The four terminals are spread along the harbour, so there is no single walk to the centre.
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: HafenCity is inside the Überseequartier complex, while Altona, Steinwerder, and Baakenhöft are separate berths along the Elbe.
gettingThere.walkingTime: From U4 Überseequartier the HafenCity terminal is a short walk inside the complex. The other terminals are not a walk from the centre.
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Taxis are available at each terminal.
gettingThere.publicTransport: For HafenCity, take the S-Bahn to Hamburg Hauptbahnhof, change to the U4 at Hauptbahnhof Nord, and ride two stops to Überseequartier.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one waterfront cluster. Cruise Center HafenCity is the berth beside Speicherstadt. Altona, Steinwerder, and Baakenhöft each need a transfer before you start sightseeing.
topThings: HafenCity waterfront walk and Elbphilharmonie plaza views
Speicherstadt canals and warehouse district (UNESCO)
Miniatur Wunderland (book timed entry; allow queue and transfer time)
Landungsbrücken and harbour ferries for an Elbe overview
St. Michaelis Church tower or Jungfernstieg / city-centre streets on lighter days
thingsToDo.shortCall: From Cruise Center HafenCity, stay in HafenCity: waterfront promenade, Elbphilharmonie exterior plaza, and a Speicherstadt canal loop. Skip Miniatur Wunderland on a tight 4–5 hour call.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Choose one realistic combination, not everything. Stay with the HafenCity waterfront and Speicherstadt, or book a timed Miniatur Wunderland visit plus a short promenade. From Altona, Steinwerder, or Baakenhöft, budget the transfer both ways before a second stop.
thingsToDo.longerCall: With 8 or more hours, pair Speicherstadt with either Miniatur Wunderland or the Landungsbrücken harbour stretch, and keep a buffer for Elbe traffic and terminal security. A shopping loop plus Miniatur Wunderland plus a cross-harbour transfer is usually too much for one call.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Check the pier name on your ticket before you leave the ship. A Speicherstadt walk is realistic from the HafenCity berth. Baakenhöft is a separate smaller-ship berth, not the Überseequartier terminal.

portInfo.description: Istanbul sits on the Bosphorus and works as both a marquee Mediterranean call and a growing homeport. For cruise passengers, the practical question is which berth and terminal entrance your ship uses today and how much time you have before all-aboard. Most large ships use Galataport İstanbul on the Karaköy waterfront—an underground cruise terminal where passport control, customs, and luggage handling sit below the promenade. When paperwork says Galataport, Istanbul cruise port, or the Meclis-i Mebusan address, that is the same modern complex—not a distant industrial port. Confirm with your cruise line if your booking lists another pier name (for example Salıpazarı or Sarayburnu on busy days). SeaDays does not assign berths. Istanbul is normally a dockside call at Galataport; do not assume a tender day unless your ship announces one.

politics.visaRequirements: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs states that foreigners arriving by cruise may be admitted without a visa for up to 72 hours for tourism, subject to permission by local security authorities. If you fly into Turkey, stay beyond 72 hours, or leave the cruise-tourism pattern, you may need an e-Visa or other visa via https://www.evisa.gov.tr only. Confirm for your nationality and itinerary with your cruise line and official sources—SeaDays does not guarantee entry.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport meeting your cruise line’s rules. Shore excursions do not change document requirements—keep required ID with you ashore. Do not rely on forum e-Visa advice instead of MFA guidance for cruise entry versus fly-in extensions.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Most calls use Galataport İstanbul; overflow names such as Salıpazarı or Sarayburnu may appear when the quay is busy—confirm daily
gettingThere.distanceToCity: You step into Karaköy at Galataport; the historic peninsula (Sultanahmet) is usually reached via T1, not a single fixed walk from every pier
gettingThere.distanceAnswer: Galataport puts you on the Karaköy waterfront. Your pier along the quay and terminal entrance (Block D when using the main building) can change with port traffic—read the ship’s daily programme or ask at the gangway before you plan transport. Ambarlı and other far-west commercial ports are not typical Istanbul cruise calls; verify urgently if your documents show them.
gettingThere.walkingTime: Karaköy, Galata Bridge viewpoints, and uphill lanes toward Galata Tower are realistic on foot; Sultanahmet is usually tram-first for time and energy
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Galataport routes taxis and coaches via underground road access; use official ranks and confirm destination before departure
gettingThere.publicTransport: Board T1 Kabataş–Bağcılar at Karaköy toward Bağcılar for Gülhane and Sultanahmet (Metro Istanbul). F2 Tünel links Karaköy and Beyoğlu for İstiklal-side exploring (İETT). Metro Istanbul publishes T1 operating hours as 06:00–00:00—treat that as the published schedule, not a guarantee; confirm same-day service before a late return. SeaDays does not publish fares—use current Istanbul transit payment rules.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one compact cluster and keep a generous return buffer—terminal security and multi-ship queues often beat the last museum minute.
topThings: Sultanahmet: Hagia Sophia or Blue Mosque plus Hippodrome circuit
Galata Tower and Galata Bridge views from Karaköy
Grand Bazaar or Spice Bazaar (allow time—or skip depth on short calls)
Bosphorus ferry from Karaköy/Eminönü when schedules fit
Galataport promenade and Karaköy café culture without crossing the peninsula
thingsToDo.shortCall: Option A — T1 from Karaköy to Sultanahmet: focus on Hagia Sophia or Blue Mosque (respect prayer times and dress codes) plus Hippodrome exteriors; skip deep Grand Bazaar time. Option B — stay in Karaköy/Galata: promenade, bridge views, Galata Tower area if ticket lines allow. Option C — ship excursion if it matches all-aboard. Do not stack Sultanahmet, full Bosphorus cruise, and bazaar depth on a 4–5 hour independent day.
thingsToDo.standardCall: With about 6–8 hours, choose one peninsula focus or one Bosphorus-side add-on—not both distant clusters. Example: Sultanahmet core plus a short Eminönü/Spice Bazaar stop, or Galata walk plus one timed museum if you already hold tickets.
thingsToDo.longerCall: With 8+ hours and a stable pier: morning Sultanahmet (timed tickets where required; confirm Topkapı hours on official sites day-of); midday Eminönü or tram-line lunch; afternoon pick one—Bosphorus ferry, Dolmabahçe/Beşiktaş via Kabataş end connections, or Grand Bazaar plus Süleymaniye quarter. Homeport embark/disembark: follow Galataport Block D and line reporting times.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Common mistakes: assuming a fixed pier without checking the programme; planning Sultanahmet and distant Bosphorus suburbs on a short call; underestimating terminal security on multi-ship days; confusing Galataport with Ambarlı; visa guesswork instead of MFA cruise-entry rules; Friday prayer surprises at active mosques; missing ship time in the bazaar. Typically not a tender port unless announced.

thingsToDo.practicalTip: Weekend turnarounds congest the PortMiami Tunnel and causeway. Arrive inside your cruise line’s check-in window with luggage already organized.

Cours Saleya — Cours Saleya, Vieux-Nice. The market street is a useful fixed meeting landmark; market days/hours vary. Allow 45 minutes; [official source](https://www.explorenicecotedazur.com/en/explore/towns-villages/coastal-area/nice/what-to-do-in-nice/).

Sainte-Réparate Cathedral — Place Rossetti, Vieux-Nice. Church entry is subject to worship; the square remains an outdoor target. Allow 35 minutes; [official source](https://www.explorenicecotedazur.com/en/explore/towns-villages/coastal-area/nice/what-to-do-in-nice/).

Vieux-Nice lanes — Old town between Place Rossetti and Cours Saleya, Nice. Choose a small loop instead of losing the return meeting point. Allow 60 minutes; [official source](https://www.explorenicecotedazur.com/en/explore/towns-villages/coastal-area/nice/what-to-do-in-nice/).

Promenade des Anglais / Rauba Capeu — Seafront at Quai Rauba Capeu and the Promenade des Anglais, Nice. A seafront walk with sun exposure, not an assurance of swimming conditions. Allow 60 minutes; [official source](https://www.explorenicecotedazur.com/en/explore/towns-villages/coastal-area/nice/what-to-do-in-nice/).

thingsToDo.practicalTip: Cruise shuttles toward the cathedral area are the default on busy days. Heat makes the long waterfront walk slower than guidebooks imply.

thingsToDo.intro: Piraeus is Athens’ cruise gate. The Acropolis area is roughly 10–13 km away—plan metro, taxi, or an organized tour, not a walk from the pier.
topThings: Acropolis and Acropolis Museum (one tightly planned visit)
Plaka / Monastiraki lanes after the site
Ancient Agora if time remains nearby
Piraeus waterfront if you stay local
Island ferries are a separate complex—do not confuse them with cruise gates
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near Piraeus or take a taxi for a single nearby highlight. A full Acropolis visit with only ~4–5 hours ashore is often too tight once port shuttles and heat are factored in.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Acropolis (early) + short Plaka walk is the standard independent plan. Use the internal port shuttle from outer berths before you start the city clock.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Add the Acropolis Museum or Ancient Agora when queues cooperate. Do not also chase distant neighborhoods or a Greek-island hop on the same call.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Midday Acropolis climbs in summer are demanding. Go early, carry water, and watch for heat-related site measures.

portInfo.description: San Juan’s forts make sense when read together: El Morro defended the sea approach and San Cristóbal the land approach. A cathedral, city gate and civic square add context without requiring a rainforest coach day. The official tourism article updated 25 August 2026 documents these landmarks, but its promotional “oldest city” superlative is not repeated here. The port operator describes Old San Juan for transit/luxury calls and Pan American as a major homeport district, while Pier 4 can also handle homeporting. Those are operating roles, not a promise of your ship’s assignment. Future redevelopment piers are not silently counted as currently usable cruise berths.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Pier 3 East — Paseo Concepción de Gracia,Old San Juan 00901
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The operator FAQ gives indicative airport drives of roughly 10 minutes to Pan American and 15 to Old San Juan, excluding clearance and variable traffic. These are not flight-connection guarantees. Pan American passengers should use a taxi/line transfer into the old city; Old San Juan passengers may begin walking after the authorised exit. The plans use 45-minute first legs and 45–60-minute last legs for either district, deliberately more than the city-core walk from Pier 3/4. Vehicle/walking blocks are editorial allowances. NPS’s visit page updated 11 August 2026 lists both forts daily 09:00–17:00. Its accessibility page, last updated 2017, describes steep ramps, an elevator at San Cristóbal, and inaccessible lower El Morro levels; confirm current routes/elevator and alerts rather than promising full step-free access.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Castillo San Felipe del Morro, El Morro, western tip of Old San Juan: Maritime defences and open Atlantic views. Allow about 120 minutes (editorial estimate). Heat, slopes and stairs; confirm accessible portions/current NPS schedule.

Castillo San Cristóbal, San Cristóbal, eastern edge of Old San Juan: The complementary land-facing fortification. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Not a quick extra photo stop if exploring tunnels/levels.

Catedral de San Juan Bautista, Catedral de San Juan, Old San Juan: A living religious landmark within the historic street grid. Allow about 40 minutes (editorial estimate). Worship can limit visitor access; respect dress and services.

Puerta de San Juan, Puerta de San Juan, western city wall, Old San Juan: A named gate/meeting point on the old waterfront edge. Allow about 30 minutes (editorial estimate). Uneven approaches; do not confuse it with the cruise terminal gate.

Plaza de Armas, Plaza de Armas, Old San Juan town-hall square: A shaded civic-history and refreshment pause. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Public square access does not include government interiors.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Tell the driver “Pan American East/West” or “Old San Juan Pier 3/4” plus ship name. “San Juan cruise terminal” is not enough.

portInfo.language: Greek; English widely spoken in tourism

facts.established: Volcanic island shaped by the Minoan-era eruption; modern tourism centered on caldera towns
facts.significance: Iconic Aegean cruise call known for caldera views, whitewashed villages, and sunsets
notableFeatures: Athinios commercial port for some coach operations
culturalHighlights: Black/red beach stops on island tours

size.portCapacity: Tender-based cruise operations at the caldera; limited alongside commercial capacity at Athinios
size.annualVisitors: A very high-volume Aegean tender call in peak season (published annual totals vary by source and year—treat “million+” claims cautiously)

climate.rainySeason: Limited summer rain; wind can be strong on the caldera edge
climate.humidity: Low humidity but intense sun on whitewashed paths
climate.description: Dry summer sun and tender/cable-car queues define the experience. Shoulder seasons often mean fewer ships and more manageable waits—still protect descent time.

politics.stability: Ordinary urban/tourist awareness applies; check local notices if demonstrations or large events affect transfer routes.
politics.visaRequirements: Greece follows Schengen / European short-stay frameworks for many travelers, but visa and passport rules depend on nationality and can change. Confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID only where your cruise line and destination authorities explicitly accept it). Shore excursions do not change document rules—keep required ID with you ashore.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Most cruise guests tender to the Old Port beneath Fira; some shore excursions use Athinios coach transfers instead
gettingThere.distanceToCity: Vertical ascent from Old Port to Fira; Oia is a further island transfer
gettingThere.walkingTime: Stairs from Old Port to Fira are steep and strenuous (hundreds of steps)
gettingThere.taxiInfo: Taxis and buses operate from Fira once you reach the clifftop
gettingThere.publicTransport: Cable car is the main bottleneck—budget queue time. Local buses link Fira with Oia and other villages Tender + cable-car queues are the main timing risk. On multi-ship days, prioritize Fira first and leave extra time to descend before tender cutoff.

thingsToDo.intro: Santorini is primarily a tender call to the Old Port (Skala) below Fira; some excursions use Athinios for coaches. Cable-car queues dominate the clock.
topThings: Fira caldera paths and viewpoints
Cable car between Old Port and Fira (or steep stairs)
Oia (needs transfer time from Fira)
Akrotiri archaeological site on coach-based plans
Local wine tasting on longer island loops
thingsToDo.shortCall: Tender up to Fira, walk the caldera edge, descend with extra queue time. Skip Oia unless you have a private transfer and a late all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Fira first. Oia is optional only with disciplined transfer timing. Do not browse endlessly before joining the cable-car line down.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Fira + Oia or an Akrotiri/wine loop can fit a long day. Athinios coach operations follow excursion plans—not the Old Port stroll.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Budget tender + cable-car queues as real attractions that consume time. On multi-ship days, prioritize getting up to Fira early and leaving extra time to descend.

portInfo.description: Marina Bay Cruise Centre Singapore is the purpose-built two-berth cruise gateway at Marina South. The operator architecture page states a 395 m pier (18 m wide) able to berth ships up to 220,000 GRT, 360 m LOA and 11.5 m draft, with 36,000 sqm terminal space and 11,700 passenger capacity, plus Green Mark certification. Global Ports Holding’s Singapore Cruise Port page lists SATS-Creuers as terminal operator, two berths, 695 m total berthing line, 11.3–11.5 m quay depth, max LOA 360 m, draught 11.3 m, ~500 m to city centre and 25 km to the airport, with no height restrictions. Singapore Cruise Centre (HarbourFront) exists as a separate MPA facility family — not treated as MBCCS here.

Arrive only in the embarkation window your line provides.

thingsToDo.intro: Southampton is the UK’s main turnaround port. “Things to do” often means embarkation logistics, a short city errand, or a London pre/post stay—not a packed transit sightseeing day.
topThings: Confirm Eastern Docks (Ocean / QEII, Dock Gate 4) vs Western Docks (City / Horizon / Mayflower, Dock Gate 10)
Ocean Village / waterfront dining near Western Docks
SeaCity Museum / Titanic exhibits on a longer free window
London by rail for pre- or post-cruise nights
New Forest or Isle of Wight only with ample free time
thingsToDo.shortCall: If you are embarking, prioritize check-in. Errands or a quick waterfront meal near Western Docks are realistic; Eastern Docks usually need a taxi for town.
thingsToDo.standardCall: A free afternoon before sailing can cover Ocean Village or SeaCity plus hotel transfer. Do not attempt a full London day and same-evening embarkation without a proven buffer.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Pre/post nights in London or a New Forest day trip work when you are not boarding the same evening. Treat dock security queues as part of the schedule.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Luggage + Dock Gate mistakes cost more time than the map implies. Match Gate 4 vs Gate 10 to your berth before ordering a taxi.

Published policy caps cruise at 8,000 passengers per day, two calls per day and seven per week, with a transition allowance for previously booked calls that may temporarily exceed those ceilings. thingsToDo.intro: Stadsgården can be walkable to Gamla Stan; Värtahamnen/Frihamnen usually need bus, metro, or taxi. Identify the terminal before planning a stroll.
topThings: Gamla Stan (Old Town) lanes and palace exteriors
Vasa Museum on Djurgården
Waterfront promenades and fika stops
ABBA Museum / Skansen on longer calls
Archipelago boats when schedules and berth location allow
thingsToDo.shortCall: From Stadsgården, walk Gamla Stan. From Värtan/Frihamnen, take transit to Old Town only—skip Djurgården museums.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Gamla Stan + Vasa Museum is a strong independent day when transfers cooperate. From Värtan, keep the plan tighter.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Add Skansen/ABBA or an archipelago hop on a long day. Still protect return time from the farther harbors.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: SL tickets cover buses/metro/trams. Do not assume every Stockholm berth is a Gamla Stan walk.

thingsToDo.shortCall: Walk into Casco Vello, sample oysters or tapas near the port, and stroll the waterfront gardens. Stay within a short walk of the maritime station.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Old town + Castro viewpoint or a longer waterfront loop still leaves time to return on foot. Add Samil beach only if your ship’s schedule is generous and taxis are quick.
thingsToDo.longerCall: Cíes Islands or Santiago are realistic only with an early start, confirmed ferry/train timing, and a disciplined return buffer. Do not stack both with a casual city walk.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Uphill lanes in Casco Vello take longer than the map suggests. Wear comfortable shoes and keep an eye on ship time even though the pier is close.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Zeebrugge Heritage Walk starts at the information panel at Rederskaai 60. The official 5.8 km route takes about two hours and returns to the terminal. It follows harbour-crane studs past fishing history and local landmarks. Verify mobility needs rather than assuming the entire route is step-free.
Markt, 8000 Brugge: allow 30–45 minutes for the square and surrounding facades. It is the orientation stop for the city, not a ticketed attraction. Leave time for uneven streets and crowds.

Belfort, Markt 7: allow 60–90 minutes only with suitable fitness and admission. There are 366 steps; this is not a step-free viewpoint. The operator recommends advance booking and says last admission is an hour before closing.

Begijnhof, 8000 Brugge: allow 30–45 minutes and visit quietly. This is an inhabited place, not an outdoor stage. The tourism board describes paths and entrance as accessible with assistance, not independently barrier-free.

Groeningemuseum, Dijver 12: allow 90 minutes for a focused art visit. The tourism board explicitly dates a four-year refurbishment closure from 11 January 2027, with core collection material planned elsewhere from March 2027. Do not reuse a 2026 itinerary after that closure without revision.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: The free port shuttle and a transfer to Bruges are different services. A ticket or statement about one does not establish price, availability or return pickup for the other.
